reason: The text depicts the tribes of Israel and the general population as actively supportive of David throughout. The tribes voluntarily approach David at Hebron, explicitly affirm him ('we are your bone and your flesh'), acknowledge his past military leadership, and formally anoint him as king. During the ark procession, the people celebrate with David through music and instruments in joyful commemoration. David distributes food gifts to all the people, and they depart peacefully to their homes. The only individual expressing antagonism is Michal (daughter of the former king Saul)—a member of the deposed royal family, not a 'regular person'—who despises David's humble dancing privately and criticizes him afterward. There is no evidence of widespread popular antagonism or resistance to David's leadership from the common people.
